issues.legal_issue: Amendments made to an enactment after its inclusion in the constitutional schedule do not receive schedule-based immunity merely because they are ancillary to provisions already included.
material_facts: The principal agricultural land-ceiling enactment, including its then-existing provisions, was included in the Ninth Schedule.
Later state amendments added or changed provisions, including provisions concerning the continued cultivation of acquired land by a state-owned farming corporation.
The later amendments were challenged as constitutionally invalid, and the High Court held that some were protected because they were ancillary or incidental to a scheduled provision.
issues.conclusion: The amendments made after the principal enactment was included in the Ninth Schedule were not protected by Article 31B, whether or not they were ancillary to provisions already protected.
issues.legal_principle: Article 31B protects the Acts, Regulations, and provisions specified in the Ninth Schedule against challenges based on Part III rights, but its protection extends only to the enactment as it stood when included, including amendments made by that time. Later amendments must be tested on their own merits; protection cannot be extended to them on the ground that they are ancillary or incidental. The Court relied on Sri Ram Ram Narain Medhi v. State of Bombay, Sajjan Singh v. State of Rajasthan, Ramanlal Gulab Chand Shah v. State of Gujarat, State of Orissa v. Chandra Sekhar Singh Bhoi, and State of Maharashtra v. Madhavrao Damodar Patilchand.

rule.if: constitutional_challenge_to_later_amendment and principal_enactment_was_previously_listed and amendment_was_made_after_listing and amendment_was_not_itself_listed

predicates.constitutional_challenge_to_later_amendm: A party challenges the constitutionality of an amendment to an enactment that had already been placed in a constitutional schedule.
predicates.principal_enactment_was_previously_liste: The principal enactment had been placed in the constitutional schedule before the challenged amendment was made.
predicates.amendment_was_made_after_listing: The challenged amendment was enacted after the principal enactment was placed in the schedule.
predicates.amendment_was_not_itself_listed: The challenged amendment was not separately placed in the constitutional schedule.

issues.definition: When a constitutional challenge concerns an amendment made after the principal enactment was listed and the amendment itself was not listed, the amendment does not receive schedule-based immunity.

issues.legal_issue: Acquisition and retention of surplus agricultural land as part of a scheme to prevent concentration of holdings and promote efficient agriculture and rural welfare is a measure of agrarian reform.
material_facts: The enactment imposed ceilings on agricultural holdings, provided for acquisition of surplus land, and provided for distribution of surplus land.
For land held by industrial undertakings and used to produce raw material, the enactment provided for maintaining the land in compact blocks and cultivating it efficiently.
Efforts to establish joint farming societies did not succeed, and the legislature provided for the land to be cultivated on a continuing basis by a state-owned farming corporation.
The stated reasons included avoiding fragmentation, enabling improvement and efficient use of the land, and maintaining the supply of agricultural raw material.
issues.conclusion: The impugned provisions, including the provision for continued cultivation of the acquired industrial land by the state-owned farming corporation, were protected by Article 31A as measures of agrarian reform.
issues.legal_principle: Article 31A protects acquisition of land when it is for agrarian reform. Agrarian reform is wider than land redistribution and includes measures to improve the rural economy and welfare; a scheme may retain particular compact tracts with the State or a state-owned corporation where that retention serves the scheme's general agrarian purpose and is not an oblique deviation from it. The Court relied on Kavalappara Kottarathil Kochuni v. State of Madras, P. Vajravelu Mudaliar v. Special Deputy Collector, Ranjit Singh v. State of Punjab, Balmadies Plantations Ltd. v. State of Tamil Nadu, Kanan Devan Hills Produce Co. Ltd. v. State of Kerala, State of Kerala v. Gwalior Rayon Silk Manufacturing (Wvg.) Co. Ltd., and Kh. Fida Ali v. State of Jammu and Kashmir.

predicates.constitutional_challenge_to_land_acquisi: A party brings a constitutional challenge to a law or measure that acquires land.
predicates.agricultural_holdings_are_subject_to_a_c: The scheme limits the amount of agricultural land a person may hold.
predicates.surplus_land_is_acquired_for_the_scheme: Land exceeding the applicable holding limit is acquired as part of the scheme.
predicates.acquired_land_is_retained_compact_for_ef: Some acquired land is kept in compact blocks and cultivated by a public body rather than distributed in the same way as other surplus land.
predicates.retention_serves_agrarian_reform_and_rur: The retention is intended to support the scheme's agricultural and rural-welfare purposes, such as preventing fragmentation and improving efficient cultivation.

issues.definition: If a land-acquisition challenge concerns a ceiling-based scheme in which surplus land is acquired and some acquired land is retained compactly for efficient cultivation in service of agrarian reform and rural welfare, the acquisition and retention are protected as agrarian reform.
